rationale: Adds an executed safety stress with a fixed seed: five real instances, randomized appends and ticks, and messages delivered or dropped from a shared queue, with every pair of decided prefixes compared after each action. The predicate is the core agreement property (equal values at every index decided on both nodes); the expectation is zero divergences under these exercised conditions, which would be a scoped negative result for decision safety and would bound the visibility defects already recorded.

scope.description: Five OmniPaxos instances, 900 randomized actions drawing appends (up to 120), ticks and message deliveries with 12 percent loss from a shared queue; decided prefixes of all ten node pairs are compared after every action.
assumptions: Messages are drawn from a shared queue and may be delivered out of order or dropped, modelling an unreliable transport.
Ticks drive BLE elections and the documented resend timers.
No snapshots, trimming or reconfiguration are used, so decided prefixes are index-aligned from 0.
excluded: Snapshots, compaction, flexible quorums, reconfiguration, crash-restart and adversarial (Byzantine) participants.

experiment.prefix: Build nodes 1..5 from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]} and settle. Seed a xorshift state. For 900 actions, pick by a random percentage: 25 percent append the next Value on a random node (up to 120 appends); 20 percent tick a random node; otherwise remove a random message from the shared queue and, with 12 percent probability, drop it, else deliver it to its addressed node. After each action collect outgoing messages into the queue, cap the queue at 4000 by dropping the oldest, then read read_decided_suffix(0) on every node and compare all pairs index by index. Emit one safety event with appended, delivered, dropped, divergences, first_divergence and the five decided indices.

comparisons.description: Agreement: no two nodes may report different values at any index both have decided.
